40.author: St. John Chrysostom
40.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew, Homily 79
40.text: Chrysostom never lets his Antiochenes leave this verse alone. Christ does not say 'in as much as ye have done it unto these, ye have honored Me' or 'pleased Me'; He says 'ye have done it unto Me.' The hungry man, the stranger, the prisoner are not occasions for the believer's good deed; they are Christ Himself standing at the door. Chrysostom drives the consequence home: there are altars in your streets, he says, more honored by God than the gold-laid altar of the basilica. They are the bodies of the poor.

40.author: St. Gregory the Theologian
40.work: Oration 14, On Love of the Poor
40.text: Gregory the Theologian uses Matthew 25 as the foundation of his sermon at a leper hospice his brother Caesarius had endowed. The lepers, he tells the wealthy of Cappadocia, are not God's failed creation; they are God's portrait of His Son. To care for them is to honor Christ in the very flesh He took for our sake. To pass them by is to refuse the Master who, on the last day, will ask not whether we believed correctly but whether we recognized Him in them.
